details.expected: Requirements. Your speed must allow a stop within the visible road and before foreseeable hazards. Darkness does not create a separate allowance to travel beyond the distance you can assess. Keep the required lamps on; daytime running lights alone may be insufficient when conditions deteriorate. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§14–15 and 68–71

details.expected: Use main beam when needed for a sufficient field of view, but not where the road is adequately lit, where it can dazzle an approaching driver or an adjacent rail/ship operator, or at close distance behind another vehicle. Dipped beam is the usual driving light. In fog or heavy precipitation, front fog lights may replace dipped beam; the prohibited combinations must not be used together. A rear fog light is restricted to fog, heavy precipitation or comparable reduced visibility and must not dazzle a following driver. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§69–72

details.expected: Learning approach. Make lighting and speed one decision. If you dip the lights and can see less far, reassess speed immediately. Check the edges of the visible road for people and animals rather than assuming a dark area is empty. Keep windows and mirrors clear enough for a useful view and learn demisting controls before a difficult journey.

Transportstyrelsen: dipped beam and front fog lights

details.expected: Central vision · Read the detail. Central vision supplies the fine detail where you are looking directly. Reading the precise wording on a road sign relies particularly on it. Merely noticing a sign at the edge of your view does not establish what its text says. Official driver-vision guidance

details.expected: Peripheral vision · Notice, then inspect. Peripheral or side vision surrounds your direct focus. It can alert you to movement, a developing hazard or a traffic change outside that focus. Move your eyes, and head where needed, to inspect the relevant object directly while maintaining control and awareness of the road. For example, notice movement near the verge, then look to identify whether it is a person about to enter your path. Keep scanning; staring at one sign can leave other information unattended. Official driver-vision guidance

details.expected: One light · Keep width uncertain. One approaching light at night does not prove a narrow motorcycle. A wider car can have a failed headlight. Transportstyrelsen documents defective car headlights; the practical inference is to allow for a vehicle whose full width is not yet visible. Preserve a safe lateral margin and adapt speed to the view rather than squeezing past on a guessed width. Transportstyrelsen: defective car headlights

details.expected: Answer: (1) No; adapt speed and gap. (2) Cold air cools it above and below. (3) A nearly invisible slippery ice layer. (4) Water mixes with accumulated dirt/oily residues. (5) To reduce rear grip loss, tail swing and rotation. (6) Oversteer: rear grip loss, tail outward, more rotation than intended. Understeer: front grip loss, less turn and a wider/straighter path. (7) A water film reduces effective tyre-road contact. Ease off the accelerator, keep steering steady and avoid abrupt steering/hard braking; use gentle necessary corrections.

details.expected: Your goal: Explain how surface conditions, tyres and driver inputs affect stability, steering and braking.
details.observed: Your goal: Explain how surface conditions, tyres and driver inputs affect stability, steering and braking.

details.expected: Tyres need friction to change the vehicle's speed and direction. Braking while cornering shares that capacity; ABS can help preserve steering forces during braking, but the available friction still limits the result. Water, snow and ice change the conditions at the tyre contact, so dry-road expectations cannot simply be carried into them. VTI friction report, sections 4.2–4.3

details.expected: Requirements for ordinary light cars and their trailers, checked 1 October 2026. Between 1 December and 31 March, winter tyres or equivalent equipment are required when winter conditions exist. Snow, ice, slush or frost on any part of the road counts; police determine conditions at the location. The minimum tread depth for the ordinary light-vehicle case is 3 mm. Studless winter tyres for the car need the mountain/snowflake marking. Winter tyres

Studless winter tyres for the car need the mountain/snowflake marking. Winter tyres

details.expected: Studded tyres are permitted from 1 October to 15 April and outside that period when winter conditions exist or are expected. Do not mix studded and non-studded tyres on an ordinary passenger car or light goods vehicle. In winter conditions, a studded towing car requires a studded trailer; the reverse combination is allowed. A light-trailer transition permits specified winter-designed M+S tyres through 30 November 2028. Exemptions and heavier-vehicle cases need their own checks; they are not the ordinary car rule. Winter tyres · Traffic Regulation, chapter 4 §§18a–18d

A legal minimum is not a promise of equal performance in every condition. Transportstyrelsen: tyres

details.expected: Surface change · A bridge can freeze first. A bridge is exposed to cold air above and below. That exposure can cool it faster than neighbouring road supported by ground, so moisture can freeze on the bridge while the approach still appears clear. It is a possibility, not a rule that every bridge always freezes first. Anticipate uncertain grip and reduce speed before reaching the bridge. National Weather Service: bridge cooling

details.expected: Rain on a cold road · Ice can hide. Rainwater can freeze when it meets a road surface cold enough for ice to form, producing a thin, nearly invisible slippery layer. The road may look wet, and the air temperature can be above zero while the surface is still below freezing. Near-zero air alone does not prove ice, but it calls for attention to surface conditions, more space and lower speed. Trafikverket: deceptive ice and cold roads

details.expected: First rain after dry weather · Residues matter. During a dry spell, dust, dirt and oily residues can accumulate. The first rain can mix with these contaminants and make the road unusually slippery. Reassess speed and separation as rain starts; do not assume a light shower immediately washes the surface clean or that a fixed time restores grip. County Fire: rain after a dry spell

details.expected: Rear stability · Why the best grip belongs at the rear. Transportstyrelsen recommends the best-grip or deepest-tread tyres at the rear to reduce skid risk in braking and bends, for both front- and rear-wheel-drive cars. Better rear grip helps reduce the risk of the rear sliding outward and rotating the car. Suitable tyres and stability assistance still cannot guarantee control. Transportstyrelsen: best tyres at the rear · VTI: rear grip and oversteer

details.expected: Oversteer · Rear grip loss. In the loss-of-grip situation, the rear tyres lose sufficient lateral grip, the tail swings outward and the car rotates more than intended into the turn. This can develop into a spin. VTI: oversteer and rear stability
details.observed: Oversteer · Rear grip loss. In the loss-of-grip situation, the rear tyres lose sufficient lateral grip, the tail swings outward and the car rotates more than intended into the turn. This can develop into a spin. VTI: oversteer and rear stability

details.expected: Understeer · Front grip loss. In the loss-of-grip situation, the front tyres cannot supply the lateral grip needed for the requested turn. The car turns less than intended and follows a straighter, wider path; adding more steering does not guarantee the requested curve. These are grip-loss explanations, not a full definition of every vehicle's normal handling characteristics. VTI: handling paths · NHTSA: front-axle grip limit

details.expected: Aquaplaning · Water interrupts contact. If water builds between tyres and road, it can support the tyre on a film and reduce or remove effective tyre-road contact. Steering and braking then have less grip to work with. Reduce speed before standing water and uncertain wet surfaces. PennDOT: aquaplaning
details.observed: Aquaplaning · Water interrupts contact. If water builds between tyres and road, it can support the tyre on a film and reduce or remove effective tyre-road contact. Steering and braking then have less grip to work with. Reduce speed before standing water and uncertain wet surfaces. PennDOT: aquaplaning

details.expected: Response · Ease off smoothly. If aquaplaning starts and there is space to slow gradually, ease off the accelerator, keep steering steady and avoid abrupt steering or hard braking. Make only gentle necessary corrections as contact returns. This is different from M02-L01's ABS emergency-stop instruction: ABS cannot create grip where a tyre is separated from the road by water. An immediate collision emergency needs action appropriate to the actual situation; this advice does not establish a universal ban on braking. PennDOT: aquaplaning response

details.expected: Worked grip comparison. A rear slide swinging the tail outward is oversteer; a front slide that prevents the intended curve is understeer. A light, unresponsive steering feel over standing water raises a different possibility: aquaplaning. Recognise the mechanism, preserve margins and practise vehicle-specific emergency handling only with suitable instruction.

details.expected: Requirements. During road travel, a driver may use communication equipment only if it does not adversely affect driving. Holding the equipment in the hand while using it is prohibited. Hands-free use is therefore not automatically acceptable: the effect on driving still matters. You must also not drive when exhaustion or another condition prevents safe control. Transportstyrelsen: communication equipment · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1 and chapter 4 §10e

expected_segments: Your goal: Choose a visibility and lighting strategy for darkness, fog and glare.

checks.name: M07-L01/teaching-002 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Requirements. Your speed must allow a stop within the visible road and before foreseeable hazards. Darkness does not create a separate allowance to travel beyond the distance you can assess. Keep the required lamps on; daytime running lights alone may be insufficient when conditions deteriorate. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§14–15 and 68–71

expected_segments: Continue the learning

checks.name: M07-L01/teaching-003 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Use main beam when needed for a sufficient field of view, but not where the road is adequately lit, where it can dazzle an approaching driver or an adjacent rail/ship operator, or at close distance behind another vehicle. Dipped beam is the usual driving light. In fog or heavy precipitation, front fog lights may replace dipped beam; the prohibited combinations must not be used together. A rear fog light is restricted to fog, heavy precipitation or comparable reduced visibility and must not dazzle a following driver. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§69–72

checks.name: M07-L01/teaching-004 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Learning approach. Make lighting and speed one decision. If you dip the lights and can see less far, reassess speed immediately. Check the edges of the visible road for people and animals rather than assuming a dark area is empty. Keep windows and mirrors clear enough for a useful view and learn demisting controls before a difficult journey.

checks.name: M07-L01/teaching-005 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Automatic lighting is an aid, not confirmation that every required lamp is on. In a car whose daytime-light mode leaves the rear lights off, check the actual setting when darkness or bad weather arrives. Transportstyrelsen: vehicle lighting

checks.name: M07-L01/production-0003 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Light and visual information

checks.name: M07-L01/teaching-006 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Lighting choice · Name the prohibited pair. Do not use dipped headlights and front fog lights together. In fog or heavy precipitation, front fog lights may replace dipped headlights; they are not an extra light to add to them. Select a permitted mode and check it on the actual vehicle. Transportstyrelsen: dipped beam and front fog lights

checks.name: M07-L01/teaching-007 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Central vision · Read the detail. Central vision supplies the fine detail where you are looking directly. Reading the precise wording on a road sign relies particularly on it. Merely noticing a sign at the edge of your view does not establish what its text says. Official driver-vision guidance

checks.name: M07-L01/teaching-008 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Peripheral vision · Notice, then inspect. Peripheral or side vision surrounds your direct focus. It can alert you to movement, a developing hazard or a traffic change outside that focus. Move your eyes, and head where needed, to inspect the relevant object directly while maintaining control and awareness of the road. For example, notice movement near the verge, then look to identify whether it is a person about to enter your path. Keep scanning; staring at one sign can leave other information unattended. Official driver-vision guidance

checks.name: M07-L01/teaching-009 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: One light · Keep width uncertain. One approaching light at night does not prove a narrow motorcycle. A wider car can have a failed headlight. Transportstyrelsen documents defective car headlights; the practical inference is to allow for a vehicle whose full width is not yet visible. Preserve a safe lateral margin and adapt speed to the view rather than squeezing past on a guessed width. Transportstyrelsen: defective car headlights

checks.name: M07-L01/production-0004 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Reassess the visible road

expected_segments: Worked decision. Rain becomes heavy during a daytime trip. The dashboard remains illuminated, but the driver checks and selects the appropriate exterior lighting rather than inferring that the rear lights must be on. The driver also reduces speed for the shorter usable view.

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-001 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Your goal: Explain how surface conditions, tyres and driver inputs affect stability, steering and braking.

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-002 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Tyres need friction to change the vehicle's speed and direction. Braking while cornering shares that capacity; ABS can help preserve steering forces during braking, but the available friction still limits the result. Water, snow and ice change the conditions at the tyre contact, so dry-road expectations cannot simply be carried into them. VTI friction report, sections 4.2–4.3

checks.name: M07-L02/production-0001 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Warnings about grip Independent slippery-road and loose-chippings warnings. Observe the actual surface; these warnings are not limited to winter.

checks.name: M07-L02/official-example-A10-1 reader content and answer reveal

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-003 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Requirements for ordinary light cars and their trailers, checked 1 October 2026. Between 1 December and 31 March, winter tyres or equivalent equipment are required when winter conditions exist. Snow, ice, slush or frost on any part of the road counts; police determine conditions at the location. The minimum tread depth for the ordinary light-vehicle case is 3 mm. Studless winter tyres for the car need the mountain/snowflake marking. Winter tyres

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-004 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Studded tyres are permitted from 1 October to 15 April and outside that period when winter conditions exist or are expected. Do not mix studded and non-studded tyres on an ordinary passenger car or light goods vehicle. In winter conditions, a studded towing car requires a studded trailer; the reverse combination is allowed. A light-trailer transition permits specified winter-designed M+S tyres through 30 November 2028. Exemptions and heavier-vehicle cases need their own checks; they are not the ordinary car rule. Winter tyres · Traffic Regulation, chapter 4 §§18a–18d

checks.name: M07-L02/production-0003 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Check local studded-tyre restrictions Seasonal permission to use studs does not override a local prohibition. This road sign is not a tyre sidewall marking.

checks.name: M07-L02/official-example-C44-1 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: The prohibition concerns motor vehicles with studded tyres. Class II mopeds are included only if a supplementary panel says so. Studded tyre crossed by a red diagonal.
No studded-tyre motor vehicles except class II mopeds. Studded tyre crossed by a red diagonal.

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-005 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: For summer conditions, the minimum tread depth is 1.6 mm. Transportstyrelsen recommends placing the tyres with the best grip or greatest tread depth at the rear and checking pressure against the vehicle's instructions. A legal minimum is not a promise of equal performance in every condition. Transportstyrelsen: tyres

checks.name: M07-L02/production-0004 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Read changing surfaces

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-007 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Surface change · A bridge can freeze first. A bridge is exposed to cold air above and below. That exposure can cool it faster than neighbouring road supported by ground, so moisture can freeze on the bridge while the approach still appears clear. It is a possibility, not a rule that every bridge always freezes first. Anticipate uncertain grip and reduce speed before reaching the bridge. National Weather Service: bridge cooling

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-008 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Rain on a cold road · Ice can hide. Rainwater can freeze when it meets a road surface cold enough for ice to form, producing a thin, nearly invisible slippery layer. The road may look wet, and the air temperature can be above zero while the surface is still below freezing. Near-zero air alone does not prove ice, but it calls for attention to surface conditions, more space and lower speed. Trafikverket: deceptive ice and cold roads

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-009 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: First rain after dry weather · Residues matter. During a dry spell, dust, dirt and oily residues can accumulate. The first rain can mix with these contaminants and make the road unusually slippery. Reassess speed and separation as rain starts; do not assume a light shower immediately washes the surface clean or that a fixed time restores grip. County Fire: rain after a dry spell

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-010 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Worked surface decision. A light shower begins after dry weather as you approach a bridge in near-freezing conditions. Plan for both wet residues and possible local ice. The clear-looking approach does not measure the grip on the bridge.

checks.name: M07-L02/production-0005 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Understand grip and handling

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-011 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Rear stability · Why the best grip belongs at the rear. Transportstyrelsen recommends the best-grip or deepest-tread tyres at the rear to reduce skid risk in braking and bends, for both front- and rear-wheel-drive cars. Better rear grip helps reduce the risk of the rear sliding outward and rotating the car. Suitable tyres and stability assistance still cannot guarantee control. Transportstyrelsen: best tyres at the rear · VTI: rear grip and oversteer

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-012 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Oversteer · Rear grip loss. In the loss-of-grip situation, the rear tyres lose sufficient lateral grip, the tail swings outward and the car rotates more than intended into the turn. This can develop into a spin. VTI: oversteer and rear stability

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-013 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Understeer · Front grip loss. In the loss-of-grip situation, the front tyres cannot supply the lateral grip needed for the requested turn. The car turns less than intended and follows a straighter, wider path; adding more steering does not guarantee the requested curve. These are grip-loss explanations, not a full definition of every vehicle's normal handling characteristics. VTI: handling paths · NHTSA: front-axle grip limit

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-014 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Aquaplaning · Water interrupts contact. If water builds between tyres and road, it can support the tyre on a film and reduce or remove effective tyre-road contact. Steering and braking then have less grip to work with. Reduce speed before standing water and uncertain wet surfaces. PennDOT: aquaplaning

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-015 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Response · Ease off smoothly. If aquaplaning starts and there is space to slow gradually, ease off the accelerator, keep steering steady and avoid abrupt steering or hard braking. Make only gentle necessary corrections as contact returns. This is different from M02-L01's ABS emergency-stop instruction: ABS cannot create grip where a tyre is separated from the road by water. An immediate collision emergency needs action appropriate to the actual situation; this advice does not establish a universal ban on braking. PennDOT: aquaplaning response

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-016 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Worked grip comparison. A rear slide swinging the tail outward is oversteer; a front slide that prevents the intended curve is understeer. A light, unresponsive steering feel over standing water raises a different possibility: aquaplaning. Recognise the mechanism, preserve margins and practise vehicle-specific emergency handling only with suitable instruction.

checks.name: M07-L02/production-0006 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Prepare before grip changes

checks.name: M07-L02/teaching-006 reader content and answer reveal

expected_segments: Learning approach. Reduce speed and increase space before reaching uncertain grip. Avoid demanding abrupt braking, steering and acceleration together. Do not experiment with skid recovery in ordinary traffic. Establish the actual vehicle's emergency-braking behaviour through appropriate instruction and risk training. Trafikverket: winter driving advice · Risk training

expected_segments: Requirements. During road travel, a driver may use communication equipment only if it does not adversely affect driving. Holding the equipment in the hand while using it is prohibited. Hands-free use is therefore not automatically acceptable: the effect on driving still matters. You must also not drive when exhaustion or another condition prevents safe control. Transportstyrelsen: communication equipment · Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §1 and chapter 4 §10e

No universal break interval in this material certifies that you can continue safely. Journey advice
